raw_segments.text: Some leases prescribe to the tenant a certain mode of cultivation and a certain succession of crops during the whole continuance of the lease.
This condition, which is generally the effect of the landlord's conceit of his own superior knowledge,
a conceit in most cases very ill-founded,
ought always to be considered as an additional rent, as a rent in service, instead of a rent in money.
In order to discourage the practice, which is generally a foolish one,
this species of rent might be valued rather high, and consequently taxed somewhat higher than common money rents.
